title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Non-reassuring fetal heart rate
decisions.scenario: Fetal monitoring shows late decelerations with each contraction.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Reposition the mother and apply oxygen.
decisions.modelNext: Stop oxytocin and notify the provider.

decisions.title: Amniotic fluid embolism
decisions.scenario: Shortly after delivery, a woman develops sudden respiratory distress, hypotension, and bleeding from IV sites.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Call a rapid response and provide supportive care.
decisions.modelWhy: Amniotic fluid embolism is a life-threatening emergency.

decisions.title: Postpartum infection
decisions.scenario: Two days after delivery, a woman has a fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Notify the provider and prepare to administer antibiotics.

decisions.title: Breast engorgement
decisions.scenario: A postpartum woman reports painful, firm breasts and difficulty breastfeeding.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Mastitis
decisions.scenario: A breastfeeding woman reports unilateral breast pain, redness, and fever.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Continue breastfeeding and notify the provider.
decisions.modelWhy: Emptying the breast helps resolve infection.

decisions.title: Postpartum depression
decisions.scenario: A woman two weeks postpartum reports persistent sadness and lack of interest in her baby.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Screen for postpartum depression and provide support.

decisions.title: Newborn hypoglycemia
decisions.scenario: A newborn of a diabetic mother is jittery and has a blood glucose of 2.2 mmol/L.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Initiate feeding or glucose therapy as ordered.

decisions.title: Newborn respiratory distress
decisions.scenario: A newborn has nasal flaring, grunting, and a respiratory rate of 70 breaths per minute.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Provide oxygen and notify the neonatal team.
